gaps.note: Tempo changed interpreter during the cycle. The critic queried web3_clientVersion at https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz on 2026-11-24 and got tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748, while stablecoin-l1 recorded tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97 as the running and newest release. The v1.19.1 lock (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/tempo/v1.19.1/Cargo.lock, compared with the v1.19.0 lock) moves evm2 and all evm2-jit crates from 66687c18 to 35aa3280, reth from 31d05e14 to 167933d1 and reth-core from 275ce4cf to 5dabd396; ruint stays at 1.21.1. The changelog page https://tempo.com/developers/docs/changelog.md still lists v1.19.0 as the newest release and has no v1.19.1 entry, and the repository has no CHANGELOG.md at the v1.19.1 tag (404). Every Tempo vector, callsem, statekeys and pmdiff result of cycle 13 therefore describes a build the endpoint no longer runs, and the evm2 diff 66687c18..35aa3280 was named in L-632 but never read.

Unichain, Ink and Soneium now answer op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332 (critic query of the endpoints in state/networks.json on 2026-11-24). No cycle has recorded rc.4 or commit 65e80332; cycle 12 read rc.1. The lock at 65e80332 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/65e80332/rust/Cargo.lock) pins the same revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, op-revm 20.0.0, ruint 1.20.0 and alloy-primitives 1.7.3 as rc.1, so the opcode handlers are probably the same. The reth engine, execution cache and prewarm code between rc.1 and rc.4 was not read, and the battery was not rerun on rc.4.

Fourteen networks had no network unit in cycle 13. On them the only new evidence is the mined-swap replay of theme-swap-residuals, plus the HyperEVM replays of theme-mined-branches. battery.py, targeted.py, callsem.py, statekeys.py and pmdiff.py were not rerun, and no release note since cycle 12 was read for reth v2.11.0, base v1.5.6 (reth v2.5.2), world-chain v2.8.2, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, celo reth v2.2.0-74cc8bb, xlayer v0.0.7, nitro, bor, BSC geth v1.8.2, avalanchego 1.15.3 or HyperEVM. The Polygon endpoint in state/networks.json (https://polygon.drpc.org) now answers Geth/v10.0.0/drpc, which hides the bor build. https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com answers bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private (critic queries, 2026-11-24). An eth_call result from the drpc endpoint therefore cannot be tied to a release.

Arc's three public endpoints report three builds: arc_getVersion v0.8.6-rc1 (37812c61) on rpc.mainnet.arc.io (critic query repeated 2026-11-24), v0.8.5 on publicnode and v0.8.6 (8e8edb7a) on dRPC (stablecoin-l1). The opcode battery and pmdiff ran only on the official endpoint. The validator set is permissioned, and no unit established which release the validators run. The v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 stale-cache fault shows that Arc releases differ in state results, so this is more than bookkeeping.

high-throughput's L-674 clearance (eth_call runs on a separate InterpreterOnly VM, monad_executor.cpp 1306-1309 at v0.16.7) means that all 185,529 vectors and the 550 to 706 pmdiff scripts ever run on Monad tested only the interpreter. The compiled path is evidenced only by transcriptions (cycles 10 to 13) and by mined replays, and the mined replays have no instance of the FullMath 512-bit branch, the SqrtPriceMath overflow fallback, clear, transferFrom or swaps ending on an initialized tick (theme-mined-branches). Whether the 24,009 byte runtime is compiled at all is still open after L-648, L-672 and L-676.

MegaETH: the mined-branch replay compares the sequencer's logs and storage with a revm re-execution for 1,566 transactions. That is the only check of the closed sequencer executor. L-626 (stateless validator) was again not run, for the fourth cycle running, and the same producer-only branch list as on Monad has no mined instance. high-throughput read only mega-evm v1.7.4 changelogs and file equality. The toolchain question (rust-lang issue 155241) has no answer.

HyperEVM got no network unit in cycle 13. Its closed validator is covered only by 2,762 mined replays, and 104 of the 324 multi-step swaps in theme-swap-residuals needed a tick spacing found by search, not read from an Initialize log. hl-node's revm and ruint versions (L-618) are still unknown.

Proof programs were tested on rebuilds, not on the artifacts that settle. Kona's handlers were run as a rustc 1.97 rebuild, and the prestate scan follows only straight-line code (theme-proof-builds-2 verifier). Base's SP1 range program was run as an RV64IM rebuild, not as the published ELF under Succinct's toolchain. For Celo and X Layer the release behind the range vkeys is unidentified.

leads.question: Tempo mainnet now runs tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 with evm2 35aa3280 (was 66687c18) and reth 167933d1. Read the evm2 diff 66687c18..35aa3280 in the instruction handlers (arithmetic, MULMOD/ADDMOD, shifts, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, EXP, comparisons), jump destination analysis, memory and MCOPY, call input and output borrowing, return data, and the TSTORE/TLOAD journal and rollback. Say whether Host::execute_call (commit 2bc0eebb, L-632) lets any precompile or system path start a frame from outside a running call. Then rerun battery.py, targeted.py, callsem.py, statekeys.py, pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py on the v1.19.1 endpoint. Also check whether the release image is built with the opt-in jit feature: bin/tempo/Cargo.toml line 155 lists default features without jit, and line 268 defines jit = tempo-evm/jit; read the Dockerfile and the release workflow at the tag.
leads.why: A live network changed its interpreter after the cycle's checks. A wrong handler or journal result would change FullMath.mulDiv, TickMath or the transient delta rollback (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) in every Tempo pool, and any user could trigger it.

leads.question: Is there any Monad RPC method that runs a call or block on the block execution VM rather than the InterpreterOnly VM of monad_executor.cpp 1306-1309, for example eth_simulateV1, debug_traceBlockByNumber, debug_traceTransaction or a block replay endpoint? If one exists, run battery.py and pmdiff6 through it on the 0.16.7 endpoint. If none exists, list the Monad mainnet transactions of any contract (for example Uniswap v3 pools that share FullMath) whose receipts carry a mulDiv with a nonzero high product word or a getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0 overflow fallback, and replay them in the reference interpreter against the receipts.
leads.why: No opcode vector has ever run on Monad's compiled path. A native-code miscompile in the 512 bit branch of FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol) or in SqrtPriceMath that only producers run would let an ordinary account move pool prices or amounts on the canonical chain.

leads.question: For the PoolManager branches with no mined MegaETH instance (the FullMath 512 bit branch at pc 22358, the SqrtPriceMath overflow fallback, clear of an exact credit, transferFrom with an allowance, swaps that end exactly on an initialized tick), find mined MegaETH transactions of other contracts that run the same operand classes (MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 and a nonzero high word, full-width DIV) and compare the sequencer's storage and logs with a revm re-execution, as theme-mined-branches did for the PoolManager.
leads.why: The sequencer executor is closed and states that it compiles. The 1,566 PoolManager replays only cover common operands. A sequencer-only result on these branches would be usable by any account and would be canonical.

leads.question: Arc v0.8.5 fixed the reth execution cache fault of reth v2.2.0 (stale cached storage for an account that a block deletes and recreates; reth PR 28148; reth v2.2.0 crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs lines 861-882). Celo answers reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, X Layer reth/v2.3.0-f60420a, MegaETH mega-reth/v2.2.3 and Base reth/v2.5.2. For each pinned reth revision, is the old branch present? Is the cache used by the sequencer's payload builder, or only by engine-tree validation on follower nodes?
leads.why: Transfer from Arc. On an L2 whose sequencer serves stale storage while the proof program (OP Succinct on Celo and X Layer, SP1/TEE on Base) does not, an ordinary account could produce a state root that the proof contradicts, which delays every withdrawal, bridged pool funds included. The sequencer could also book a stale balanceOf read through sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288).

leads.question: What changed in op-reth between v2.10.0-rc.1 and v2.10.0-rc.4 (commit 65e80332) in the engine tree, execution cache, prewarming and op-revm handler, and do battery.py, targeted.py and pmdiff.py on the three endpoints that now report rc.4 still give the published results?
leads.why: Unrecorded version drift on three networks. The integer and interpreter pins are unchanged, so a difference would come from the state and cache layer.

leads.question: Which wasmModuleRoot does the Arbitrum One rollup (and the Robinhood Chain rollup) use today, read by eth_call on Ethereum? Which public consensus release (consensus-vNN) publishes that module root, and which go-ethereum commit does that release's replay binary pin?
leads.why: The rc.9 node source is private (L-677), but the binary that settles disputes has to be public for validators to check it. Its go-ethereum pin is the arithmetic that decides the state that settles, and it can be read without the private tag.
